subject: Review: CleverDrop trial grants — rotating IPs & manual issuance
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09 08:12 PST
Subject: Suspicious cluster: CleverDrop trial grants — request for triage

Hi Kimberly,

Flagging a suspicious pattern affecting CleverDrop trial grants (related HubSpot HD-2026-00472). We see ~18 free-credit grants tied to variants of "cleverdrop" email usernames across several domains (cleverdrop.com, clever-drop.net, cleverdrop-testing.io). Two signals that worry me:

- Rotating outbound IPs: requests originated from ~7 distinct /24s across multiple cloud providers (DigitalOcean and Hetzner ranges) within a 6-hour window on 2026-12-08.
- Device fingerprints and UA churn: automated UA strings, no persistent cookies in the session logs, and inconsistent timezone offsets.

I've attached signup-logs-2026-12-09.csv with the raw events (timestamp, ip, device_hash, email, token_issued). A quick look: 12 of the accounts used disposable or catch-all patterns, 6 re-used the same phone number (different formatting).

Recommendation: place a temporary hold on further auto-grants to the CleverDrop-related identifiers and route any manual issuance through sales/legal. I can run a deeper correlation (passport/hash overlaps) if we want to avoid a false positive — possible internal QA/tests could explain this.

Questions for you:
- Kimberly, do we want to pause auto-issuance for this HubSpot record while we triage?
- Dev, can you surface account creation metadata and any existing CS notes?

If we pause and it turns out to be legitimate, we can do a one-time manual grant. If it's abuse, we should block the patterns and mark the HubSpot company as suspect.

Thanks,
Aditya
Fraud & Abuse Analyst
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Julian Alvarez <julian@cleverdrop.com>
Date: 2026-12-09 09:05 PST
Subject: Re: Suspicious cluster: CleverDrop trial grants — request for triage

Thanks for the heads up, Aditya.

On Wed, Dec 9, 2026 at 08:12 AM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com> wrote:
> Flagging a suspicious pattern affecting CleverDrop trial grants...

Julian — copying you so we can resolve quickly. We received an internal signal that several trial grants tied to CleverDrop/related email patterns look automated. Before we escalate to account blocking, can you confirm whether these were internal QA/test accounts? If so, would it be possible to share:

- A quick note on why multiple domains/usernames were used
- Any internal test plan or a single verification file (org-approved)

Neha/Dev: please hold any further self-serve credit issuance to this account and put an active hold on the auto-grant rule for the HubSpot record until we clear.

If the customer confirms these are legitimate internal tests, I propose a manual, one-time 200-credit issuance while we whitelist the domain after verification. If this looks like abuse, we'll block the patterns and revoke credits issued.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Julian Alvarez <julian@cleverdrop.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09 12:30 PST
Subject: Re: Suspicious cluster: CleverDrop trial grants — request for triage

Hi Kimberly, Aditya, Neha — thanks for the ping.

Sorry for the confusion — we did run an internal QA sweep yesterday as we were stress-testing our onboarding flow ahead of a product demo. That led to many test accounts being created across a handful of subdomains (we spin up ephemeral workers that create accounts).

I've attached our "cleverdrop-internal-test-plan.pdf" which explains the test creates and the rationale. We can also verify via a billing address and GSuite domain validation if that helps. Our billing team (billing@cleverdrop.com) is on copy.

Request: we'd appreciate a small, manual grant to continue the demo next week. If you need a signed attestation, I can get one over.

— Julian
CTO, CleverDrop, Inc.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Julian Alvarez <julian@cleverdrop.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10 07:42 PST
Subject: Re: Suspicious cluster: CleverDrop trial grants — risk assessment and recommendation

Thanks for the quick reply and the test plan, Julian — that doc helps. I pulled a deeper correlation overnight. Findings:

- IP analysis: 14 of the 18 signups did use rotating cloud IPs typical of ephemeral test runners; however 4 signups match patterns we frequently see in abuse (disposable email + no user agent variability).
- Phone/email overlap: 6 accounts reused the same phone number; formatting suggests a pasted list rather than unique numbers.
- Behavioral: the session durations were under 20s for most signups, with identical initial API call patterns.

Conclusion: mixed signals. There is legitimate internal QA activity, but we also have a subset that looks like automated abuse. My recommendation is:

1) Revoke credits on the 4 accounts flagged as probable abuse (we can identify by ID in the attached fraud_summary_20261209.pdf).
2) Offer CleverDrop a one-time manual grant of 200 credits for demo purposes conditioned on either:
   - GSuite domain verification OR
   - A signed attestation from an officer of CleverDrop (DocuSign link below).
3) Add a temporary exception rule that still enforces a throttle (1 trial grant per billing domain per 24h) to prevent repeat bursts.

If they provide domain verification quickly we can whitelist and issue the 200 credits the same day. If not, hold until we get the attestation.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/sign/AXY-verify

I can take the action to revoke the 4 accounts if you approve.

Aditya
Fraud & Abuse Analyst

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Julian Alvarez <julian@cleverdrop.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-10 11:08 PST
Subject: Re: Suspicious cluster: CleverDrop trial grants — rotating IPs & manual issuance

Julian — appreciate the quick turnaround and the test plan.

Let's do the compromise Aditya suggested: once we receive either GSuite verification or the signed attestation we'll issue a one-time 200-credit manual grant. Neha, please prepare the manual grant flow and hold any further auto-issuance. Aditya, please proceed to revoke credits on the 4 accounts listed in the fraud summary.

Julian — if you can push the DocuSign back to us by EOD tomorrow I will approve the credits immediately. If you prefer domain verification, share the DNS TXT we'll look for and Dev will confirm.

Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
